verses.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸੇ ਜਲ ਸਿੰਚ ਸਿੰਚ ਕਾਸਟ ਸਮਥ ਕੀਨੇ ਜਲ ਸਨਬੰਧ ਪੁਨਿ ਬੋਹਿਥਾ ਬਿਸ੍ਵਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaise jal si(n)ch si(n)ch kaasaT samath keene jal sanaba(n)dh pun bohithaa bisavaiaas hai ||

en.bdb: Just as wood is strengthened by drenching it in water for long and then its relation with water by which a faith develops that water will not sink the wood since it has brought it, up; ships are made with it that sail across the sea.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਵਨ ਪ੍ਰਸੰਗ ਸੋਈ ਕਾਸਟ ਸ੍ਰੀ-ਖੰਡ ਹੋਤ ਮਲਯਾ ਗਿਰ ਬਾਸਨਾ ਸੁ ਮੰਡ ਪਰਗਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: pavan prasa(n)g soiee kaasaT sree-kha(n)dd hot malayaa gir baasanaa su ma(n)dd paragaas hai ||

en.bdb: The fragrance of sandalwood of Malay mountain causes happiness. The woods and plants that have been touched by that fragrant breeze also acquire the fragrance of sandalwood.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਾਵਕ ਪਰਸ ਭਸਮੀ ਕਰਤ ਦੇਹ ਗੇਹ  ਮਿਤ੍ਰ ਸਤ੍ਰ ਸਗਲ ਸੰਸਾਰ ਹੀ ਬਿਨਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: paavak paras bhasamee karat dheh geh  mitr satr sagal sa(n)saar hee binaas hai ||

en.bdb: The same wood reduces houses to ashes when it unites with fire. It also consumes friends, enemies and the whole world.

verses.gurmukhi: ਤੈਸੇ ਆਤਮਾ ਤ੍ਰਿਗੁਨ ਤ੍ਰਿਬਿਧ ਸਕਲ ਸਿਵ ਸਾਧ ਸੰਗ ਭੇਟਤ ਹੀ ਸਾਧ ਕੋ ਅਭਿਆਸ ਹੈ ॥੬੨੫॥
verses.translit_en: taise aatamaa tiragun tirabidh sakal siv saadh sa(n)g bheTat hee saadh ko abhiaas hai ||625||

en.bdb: Just as wood interacts with water, wind, and fire differently, the human soul deals with Rajo, Tamo, and Sato differently. But by meeting with the True Guru and practicing his teachings, one becomes perfect and blissful. (625)
